text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Without U.S. presence in Bosnia, as a factor of stability, we can neither escape the crisis nor the imperialistic ambitions of certain countries in the region, Moslem co-prime minister Haris Silajdzic said upon accepting a $71 million U.S. donation for country's reconstruction.
- This is a proof that we strongly support unified Bosnia, charge d'affairs of U.S. embassy in Bosnia Michael Parmley says after signing the $71 million donation for Bosnia.
- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation government proposes a draft of law against smoking at public places such as schools and health institutions. Fines of 30 German Marks suggested for violators.
- The federation government adopts a 580 million German marks budget for 1997 which is one of conditions for donors conference in Brussels, finance minister Drago Bilandzija says.

- Moslem chairman of Bosnia's three-man presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, left for United States Thursday to receive an award for development of democracy by American Center for Democracy from Washington D.C.

- Recent newspaper poll showed one fifth of Bosnian Moslems think they should ask for their part of the country. It shows that one of the most painful taboos for Moslems, division of Bosnia, is now lifted, daily says in a commentary.

- Although the Balkan region is unsafe for long-term investments we believe that Bosnia has overcome the crisis, Christine Wallich, World bank's Bosnia director, says. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
